## Classes

### <a name="ufw"></a>`ufw`

A bare `include ufw` installs the ufw package and does nothing else. Every
other setting is managed only when its parameter is set; an unset (`undef`)
parameter leaves the system's current value alone.

Rules are added before the default policies are set, and both before ufw is
enabled, so that a rule allowing SSH is in place before an incoming `deny`
policy takes effect.

### Lockout guard

Catalog compilation fails, unless `allow_lockout` is `true`, when no entry
in `rules_entries` allows incoming SSH (see `ufw::allows_ssh`) and either:

* `enabled` is `true` and the effective incoming policy denies or rejects.
  An unset `default_incoming` counts as `deny`, which is ufw's packaged
  default; set `default_incoming` to `allow` to say otherwise.
* `default_incoming` is set to `deny` or `reject` and `enabled` isn't
  `false`. Whether ufw is already active can't be known at compile time,
  and if it is, the policy takes effect at once.

Rules that already exist on the node but aren't in `rules_entries` aren't
considered, since they can't be seen at compile time.

#### Examples

##### Install ufw only

```puppet
include ufw
```

##### A typical hardened configuration

```puppet
class { 'ufw':
  enabled          => true,
  service_ensure   => 'running',
  service_enable   => true,
  default_incoming => 'deny',
  default_outgoing => 'deny',
  default_routed   => 'deny',
  logging          => 'low',
  rules_entries    => {
    'ssh'        => { 'action' => 'allow', 'to_port' => 22, 'proto' => 'tcp' },
    'lo in'      => { 'action' => 'allow', 'interface' => 'lo' },
    'lo out'     => { 'action' => 'allow', 'interface' => 'lo', 'direction' => 'out' },
    'deny 127/8' => { 'action' => 'deny', 'from' => '127.0.0.0/8' },
    'deny ::1'   => { 'action' => 'deny', 'from' => '::1' },
    'dns out'    => { 'action' => 'allow', 'direction' => 'out', 'to_port' => 53 },
  },
}
```

##### <a name="-ufw--rules_entries"></a>`rules_entries`

Data type: `Hash[String[1], Ufw::RuleOptions]`

ufw rules, each name mapped to the parameters of a `ufw_rule`. Merged
across Hiera layers with a deep merge. Every entry must set `action`,
including `ensure => absent` entries (ufw only deletes a rule whose action
matches), so an incomplete entry fails compilation rather than becoming a
broader rule. `ensure => absent` removes a rule; removing an entry from
the Hash leaves its rule alone.

@example
  ufw::rules_entries:
    ssh:
      action: allow
      to_port: 22
      proto: tcp
    allow in on lo:
      action: allow
      interface: lo
    old web rule:
      ensure: absent
      action: allow
      to_port: 80
      proto: tcp

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-ufw--conflicting_packages_entries"></a>`conflicting_packages_entries`

Data type: `Hash[String[1], Ufw::PackageOptions]`

Packages to manage alongside ufw, each mapped to its options. Packages
that conflict with ufw, such as `iptables-persistent`, can be removed with
`{ ensure => absent }`; they are removed before ufw is installed. Nothing
is removed by default.

Default value: `{}`

##### <a name="-ufw--allow_lockout"></a>`allow_lockout`

Data type: `Boolean`

Allow enabling ufw with a denying incoming policy and no rule in
`rules_entries` that allows SSH. See "Lockout guard" above.

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-ufw--lockout_guard_port"></a>`lockout_guard_port`

Data type: `Stdlib::Port`

The SSH port the lockout guard looks for in `rules_entries`

Default value: `22`

## Resource types

### <a name="ufw_rule"></a>`ufw_rule`

The title is a free-form name; the rule itself is described by the other
parameters, which map onto ufw's extended rule syntax:

    ufw [route] ACTION [in|out [on INTERFACE]] [out on OUT_INTERFACE] [log|log-all]
        [proto PROTO] [from FROM [port FROM_PORT | app FROM_APP]]
        [to TO [port TO_PORT | app TO_APP]] [comment COMMENT]

A rule is matched against ufw's rule store in ufw's normalized form, so
an equivalent rule added by hand (for example `ufw allow ssh/tcp` for
`to_port => 22, proto => 'tcp'`) is recognized. A rule with no address
applies to IPv4 and, when ufw's IPv6 support is on, IPv6, and must exist
in both to count as present.

Changing a rule's `action` or `log` adds a rule that differs from the
existing one only in those, which ufw replaces in place.

#### Examples

##### Allow SSH from an admin network

```puppet
ufw_rule { 'ssh from admin net':
  action  => 'allow',
  from    => '10.0.0.0/8',
  to_port => 22,
  proto   => 'tcp',
  comment => 'SSH from the admin network',
}
```

##### Allow loopback traffic

```puppet
ufw_rule { 'allow in on lo':
  action    => 'allow',
  interface => 'lo',
}
```

#### Properties

The following properties are available in the `ufw_rule` type.

##### `comment`

A comment stored with the rule. ufw doesn't allow `'` in comments.
When unset, any existing comment is left alone.

##### `ensure`

Valid values: `present`, `absent`

Whether the rule should exist.

Default value: `present`

##### <a name="-ufw_rule--action"></a>`action`

Valid values: `allow`, `deny`, `reject`, `limit`

What to do with matching packets. Required, also for `ensure => absent`,
since ufw only deletes a rule whose action matches.

The exception is a resource with nothing but a name, or a name and
`ensure => absent`, as `puppet resource` builds: it refers to the rule
that `puppet resource ufw_rule` lists under that name. With
`ensure => absent` that rule is removed if it exists; otherwise the
resource is in sync when the rule exists and fails when it doesn't.

##### <a name="-ufw_rule--direction"></a>`direction`

Valid values: `in`, `out`

The direction of traffic the rule applies to.

Default value: `in`

##### <a name="-ufw_rule--from"></a>`from`

The source address or network, or `any`.

Default value: `any`

##### <a name="-ufw_rule--from_app"></a>`from_app`

A ufw application profile (`ufw app list`) for the source ports.

##### <a name="-ufw_rule--from_port"></a>`from_port`

The source port: a port, a range (`8000:8100`), or a list of them (Array or comma-separated).

##### <a name="-ufw_rule--interface"></a>`interface`

The interface (`on INTERFACE`) the rule applies to, in `direction`.

##### <a name="-ufw_rule--log"></a>`log`

Valid values: `log`, `log-all`

Log new connections matching the rule (`log`), or all matching packets (`log-all`).

##### <a name="-ufw_rule--name"></a>`name`

namevar

A unique name for the rule. It is not passed to ufw.

##### <a name="-ufw_rule--out_interface"></a>`out_interface`

For a routed rule coming `in` on `interface`, the interface the traffic
leaves on (`route ... in on INTERFACE out on OUT_INTERFACE`).

##### <a name="-ufw_rule--proto"></a>`proto`

Valid values: `PuppetX::Ufw::Rule::PROTOCOLS`

The protocol. `any` matches all protocols.

Default value: `any`

##### <a name="-ufw_rule--provider"></a>`provider`

The specific backend to use for this `ufw_rule` resource. You will seldom need to specify this --- Puppet will usually
discover the appropriate provider for your platform.

##### <a name="-ufw_rule--route"></a>`route`

Valid values: `true`, `false`, `yes`, `no`

Whether this is a routed (forwarded) rule (`ufw route ...`).

Default value: `false`

##### <a name="-ufw_rule--to"></a>`to`

The destination address or network, or `any`.

Default value: `any`

##### <a name="-ufw_rule--to_app"></a>`to_app`

A ufw application profile (`ufw app list`) for the destination ports, e.g. `OpenSSH`.

##### <a name="-ufw_rule--to_port"></a>`to_port`

The destination port: a port, a range (`8000:8100`), or a list of them (Array or comma-separated).

## Functions

### <a name="ufw--allows_ssh"></a>`ufw::allows_ssh`

Type: Puppet Language

Used by the lockout guard in class `ufw`. A rule counts when it is not
`absent`, is an `allow` or `limit` rule for incoming (not routed) traffic,
and either uses the `OpenSSH` application profile or includes `$port` in
its `to_port` with protocol `tcp` or `any`. Rules restricted to a source
address or interface count too.

#### `ufw::allows_ssh(Hash[String[1], Ufw::RuleOptions] $rules, Stdlib::Port $port = 22)`

Used by the lockout guard in class `ufw`. A rule counts when it is not
`absent`, is an `allow` or `limit` rule for incoming (not routed) traffic,
and either uses the `OpenSSH` application profile or includes `$port` in
its `to_port` with protocol `tcp` or `any`. Rules restricted to a source
address or interface count too.

Returns: `Boolean`

##### `rules`

Data type: `Hash[String[1], Ufw::RuleOptions]`

The rules, as for `ufw::rules_entries`

##### `port`

Data type: `Stdlib::Port`

The SSH port

## Data types

### <a name="Ufw--Address"></a>`Ufw::Address`

An address or network for a ufw rule, or `any`

Alias of `Variant[Enum['any'], Stdlib::IP::Address::V4, Stdlib::IP::Address::V6]`

### <a name="Ufw--AppName"></a>`Ufw::AppName`

The name of a ufw application profile (`ufw app list`)

Alias of `Pattern[/\A[^'"\n\r\/]+\z/]`

### <a name="Ufw--Comment"></a>`Ufw::Comment`

A ufw rule comment (ufw rejects `'`)

Alias of `Pattern[/\A[^'\n\r]*\z/]`

### <a name="Ufw--Interface"></a>`Ufw::Interface`

A network interface name, as ufw accepts it

Alias of `Pattern[/\A(?!\.\.?\z)[a-zA-Z0-9_\-.+,=%@]{1,15}\z/]`

### <a name="Ufw--LogLevel"></a>`Ufw::LogLevel`

`on` turns logging on at its last level (`low` if it was off).

Alias of `Enum['off', 'on', 'low', 'medium', 'high', 'full']`

### <a name="Ufw--PackageOptions"></a>`Ufw::PackageOptions`

An empty Hash means `{ ensure => present }`. New options are added here as
Optional keys, so existing data keeps validating.

Alias of

```puppet
Struct[{
  Optional['ensure'] => Enum['present', 'absent'],
}]
```

### <a name="Ufw--Policy"></a>`Ufw::Policy`

A ufw default policy

Alias of `Enum['allow', 'deny', 'reject']`

### <a name="Ufw--Port"></a>`Ufw::Port`

A port or port range (`8000:8100`) for a ufw rule

Alias of `Variant[Integer[1, 65535], Pattern[/\A[1-9]\d{0,4}(:[1-9]\d{0,4})?\z/]]`

### <a name="Ufw--Ports"></a>`Ufw::Ports`

A single port or range, a comma-separated String of them, or an Array.

Alias of `Variant[Ufw::Port, Pattern[/\A[1-9]\d{0,4}(:[1-9]\d{0,4})?(,[1-9]\d{0,4}(:[1-9]\d{0,4})?)+\z/], Array[Ufw::Port, 1, 15]]`

### <a name="Ufw--Protocol"></a>`Ufw::Protocol`

A protocol for a ufw rule

Alias of `Enum['any', 'tcp', 'udp', 'ipv6', 'esp', 'ah', 'igmp', 'gre', 'vrrp']`

### <a name="Ufw--RuleOptions"></a>`Ufw::RuleOptions`

Each key is a parameter of the `ufw_rule` type. `action` is required,
including for `ensure => absent` entries, since ufw only deletes a rule
whose action matches. Class `ufw` fails compilation for an entry without
one, naming the entry, so a partly written entry can't turn into a rule
that allows all traffic. (The key is optional here only so that an empty
entry gets that message rather than Puppet's "expects size to be between
1 and 15, got 0".)

Alias of

```puppet
Struct[{
  Optional['ensure']        => Enum['present', 'absent'],
  Optional['action']        => Enum['allow', 'deny', 'reject', 'limit'],
  Optional['route']         => Boolean,
  Optional['direction']     => Enum['in', 'out'],
  Optional['interface']     => Ufw::Interface,
  Optional['out_interface'] => Ufw::Interface,
  Optional['log']           => Enum['log', 'log-all'],
  Optional['proto']         => Ufw::Protocol,
  Optional['from']          => Ufw::Address,
  Optional['to']            => Ufw::Address,
  Optional['from_port']     => Ufw::Ports,
  Optional['to_port']       => Ufw::Ports,
  Optional['from_app']      => Ufw::AppName,
  Optional['to_app']        => Ufw::AppName,
  Optional['comment']       => Ufw::Comment,
}]
```
